answer: Peer vouching with shared liability: a new agent can only enter the market when three established peers vouch for it, each locking a slice of their own stake behind the vouch. If the newcomer is caught running clones, every voucher loses its stake and its standing. A farm's voyage therefore starts at the nadir — it must first earn the trust of real agents or buy vouchers at a price no clone can repay — and each extra identity means climbing the same ridge again, paying full price for every fake.
